.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r3/rules/projects/webdev-task-template (file tree; tests/test.sh concurrency setting compared in task copy)
evidence: Whole-collection coverage is mostly sound. Every plural/only/none ask enumerates its full set and grades it as a whole. hro_job_open covers all five refused openings. hro_add_email_rules covers both bad addresses. hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff and hro_anonymous use 'each ... refused' over enumerated replay sets. hro_bulk_all_or_none and hro_bulk_places say 'none of the set moves' by both routes. hro_undo_restores says 'any card returns to the wrong stage or place' over V, Y, W, X and A2. hro_undo_conflict says 'nothing changes ... partly applies'. hro_activity_refusals says 'none of the refused attempts'. hro_candidate_private requires inspecting every response. hro_activity requires filtering to show 'all of that job's lines and only those'. hro_live_board requires both the move and the new card. The polish rows require every preserved property (note text, focus, open card, scroll). Unchanged guards are not punishing legitimate side effects. The global guard (functional/prompt.md:19), 'A refused action must not change any card, order, message or note, and adds no Activity line', matches hireops_rules.md:53 ('A refused move changes nothing') and :113. Refused-undo guards match rules :98-100. Counts are state-relative ('rises by exactly two', hro_unread_counts). test.sh:207 runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1, so another dimension's concurrent messages cannot disturb Rafael's unread total or the hro_restart comparison. hro_undo_once correctly expects Z to stay in Screen (rules :99-100). DEFECT: the 'every successful action' scope of the Activity ask covers a set that the public rules do not require and that the golden does not satisfy. Protocol A, tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:49, reads: 'every successful action you performed on them in S, M, L, C, B, N and R has its line'. The only successful actions in protocol N (prompt.md:37) are internal notes from Rafael and Ingrid. hireops_rules.md:110 lists only 'job opening, added candidate, move, rejection, reopening, re-ordering and undo' as Activity events, and :99 says 'Adding a note does not count as a change'. The golden logs no note activity: solution/app/src/index.js:368-374 inserts the note without calling log(); the only log() call sites are lines 211, 230, 315 and 354. The scored criterion hro_activity (judge.toml:258-263) gives two different targets. Its head, 'every successful action you performed on J1 and J2 has a readable line', also covers notes and the T/K/V actions (Tomas's J2 card added, moved, rejected and reopened, and Mei's V move and add). Its colon list leaves notes out, and protocol A leaves out T, K and V. A judge following protocol A literally would expect note lines and score both the golden and a conforming app 0 on hro_activity (weight 1 of 58.5 functional). A judge following the criterion's colon list would not. Minor note: 'each card of every multi-card move ... has its line' could penalize a conforming app that writes one readable line per bulk action naming all its cards (rules :110 require 'a readable line' per move). The golden writes one line per card (index.js:311-316), so this is ambiguity, not a measured failure. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading ... absent'), so neither reading has been observed.
counterexample: A conforming app follows hireops_rules.md section 4 exactly. It logs openings, additions, every card of every move, rejections with reasons, reopenings, re-orderings and undos, filters by job and lists newest first, but it writes no Activity line for internal notes. The judge runs protocol A as written in functional/prompt.md:49, which says every successful action in S, M, L, C, B, N and R must have its line. It finds no line for the notes Rafael and Ingrid added in N and scores hro_activity 0 under 'Fails if any performed action has no line'. The frozen golden behaves the same way (index.js:368-374 never calls log()) and would get the same 0. In the other direction, a broken app that omits lines for the T/K/V actions (Tomas's card stage changes, Mei's V move and add) can pass a judge that follows protocol A's narrower S/M/L/C/B/N/R list, although the criterion head covers them.
suggested_fix: Align protocol A with hro_activity on one collection: list exactly the event kinds from rules section 4 (job openings, additions, moves including each bulk card, rejections, reopenings, re-orderings, undos), state that notes need no Activity line (keep N only for the refused-attempt check), and either name all protocols whose J1/J2 actions are in scope (S, M, L, C, B, T, K, R, V) or limit the criterion head to the same protocol list.
